verification.summary: The prior buffer-cap blocker is fixed via MOCK_GITHUB_BUFFER_CAP, but the ACCS never checks the terminal actually prints the comment-added log line, which accs.md explicitly asks for.

mustFix.quote: Check if the first issue logs that it has one comment.
mustFix.problem: accs.bash only re-fetches GET /issues and counts the array after the curl POST — it never greps mock-github.log for the contract's "[comment] issue #<id> +1 from <author>" line. A mock service that silently mutates state without ever printing that log line would still pass.

shouldFix.problem: Contract states the default port is 4000, but accs.bash's own fallback default is 4100. It's harmless since the script always exports MOCK_GITHUB_PORT before use, but the mismatch is confusing and worth aligning.

shouldFix.quote: for(const b of blocks) console.log('n='+b.n+' ids='+b.ids.length+' trunc='+b.truncated);
shouldFix.problem: scan_snapshots computes per-block line counts and a truncated flag but nothing in accs.bash asserts lines stay under the active cap or that truncation renders correctly — the buffer-cap behaviour is set to 500 purely to avoid tripping truncation, never actually exercised as a pass/fail check. Acceptable since accs.md doesn't demand testing truncation itself, but worth knowing it's untested.

shouldKnow.problem: Spec 001's ACCS runs as a synchronous foreground call rather than a backgrounded, explicitly-killed process, so "terminate only the 001 script" is satisfied by the script exiting on its own rather than by an explicit kill. Reasonable given 001's script is self-contained, just flagging the interpretation.
